q: The production of new organisms from the existing organisms of the same species is called reproduction.
e: True. The production of new organisms from the existing organisms of the same species is called reproduction. Reproduction makes a new generation so the species can continue.

q: Asexual reproduction in plants occurs through binary fission, budding, fragmentation, spore formation, and vegetative propagation.
e: True. Asexual reproduction in plants occurs through binary fission, budding, fragmentation, spore formation, and vegetative propagation. Binary fission is how many bacteria split into two similar cells.

q: A new individual produced from two parents is called asexual reproduction.
e: False. It is not true that a new individual produced from two parents is called asexual reproduction. A new individual produced from two parents is not called asexual reproduction.

q: Fission is a type of asexual reproduction that occurs in multicellular organisms only.
e: False. It is not true that fission is a type of asexual reproduction that occurs in multicellular organisms only. Fission is a type of asexual reproduction that occurs in multicellular organisms not only, so the real range is wider.

q: In budding, a small part of the body of the parent organism grows out as a bud which then detaches and becomes a new organism.
e: True. In budding, a small part of the body of the parent organism grows out as a bud which then detaches and becomes a new organism. In budding, a small outgrowth of the parent detaches and becomes a new individual.

q: Fragmentation is when the parent organism splits into two or more fragments, each fragment grows to form a new complete organism.
e: True. Fragmentation is when the parent organism splits into two or more fragments, each fragment grows to form a new complete organism. That is how this part of the lesson is stated.

q: Spore formation involves the parent plant producing many microscopic reproductive units called seeds.
e: False. It is not true that spore formation involves the parent plant producing many microscopic reproductive units called seeds.

q: Vegetative propagation involves obtaining new plants from the parts of old plants without the help of any reproductive organ.
e: True. Vegetative propagation involves obtaining new plants from the parts of old plants without the help of any reproductive organ. An organ is made of tissues that combine to do a job, such as the heart or a leaf.

q: In artificial methods of vegetative propagation, new plants are obtained from seeds.
e: False. It is not true that in artificial methods of vegetative propagation, new plants are obtained from seeds. In artificial methods of vegetative propagation, new plants are not obtained from seeds.

q: Micropropagation is the process of growing many plants from one plant by man-made methods.
e: True. Micropropagation is the process of growing many plants from one plant by man-made methods. That is how this part of the lesson is stated.
